basis: Glomangiomyoma arising in skin; vascular differentiation does not establish systemic cardiovascular disease.
Inherited skeletal dysplasia defined by shortening and abnormal development of limb bones.
ZC4H2-associated neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by congenital contractures, motor impairment and muscle abnormalities.
Filarial infection; microfilaremia alone does not establish blood damage. No additional organ has established common damaging involvement.
Defined by hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, anosmia and spastic paraplegia. Renal agenesis lacks evidence of frequency above 30%.
Interferon-mediated encephalopathy; thrombocytopenia 12/17 and inflammatory chilblains 40/90. Hepatic abnormalities (~32-47%) omitted by cap.
Joint and skin fragility define disease. HPO reports valve prolapse and rectal prolapse/malabsorption at 30-79%; frequent nerve-conduction abnormalities omitted by cap.
Mitochondrial myopathy with lactic acidosis; renal insufficiency and cardiomyopathy each 30-79%. Frequent developmental impairment omitted by cap; liver failure <30%.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss caused by TMC1 dysfunction.
Postsynaptic neuromuscular junction disorder; skeletal muscle atrophy occurs in 30-79%. Ophthalmoparesis reflects neuromuscular dysfunction; respiratory complications <30%.
Inherited melanin metabolism disorder affecting ocular pigmentation and visual development; cutaneous involvement is not defining.
Inherited susceptibility specifically targets intracerebral hemorrhage; the label identifies the target organ without assuming hemorrhage has occurred.
Mitochondrial encephalomyopathy with lactic acidosis and stroke-like episodes. Hearing loss affects roughly 50-75% of MELAS patients; MTTQ-specific frequencies are uncertain.
Congenital sensorineural hearing loss with cochlear and vestibular malformations in 2/2 patients; cochlear nerve aplasia belongs to the hearing apparatus.
Inherited retinal vascularization disorder with vitreoretinal damage. Hearing, neurologic and skeletal abnormalities are each occasional, below 30%.
Tuberculous infection of the ovary. Reproductive location has no axis; ovarian endocrine failure is not established as a defining or common feature.
Familial sebaceous gland hyperplasia produces cutaneous papules.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability commonly characterize 10p deletions. Parathyroid, renal, hearing and cardiac abnormalities depend on the deleted segment.
Ovarian endocrine failure with low estradiol, elevated gonadotropins and delayed puberty in 3/3 patients. Delayed skeletal maturation alone does not establish bone damage.
Viral infection causing meningitis or meningoencephalitis. Congenital ocular injury does not establish common ocular involvement across the disease.
Carcinoma originates in breast, outside the axes. Neuroendocrine differentiation alone does not establish endocrine gland disease or hormone dysfunction.
Inherited LDL cholesterol metabolism disorder. Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease is a separately diagnosed consequence; corneal arcus is non-damaging.
Isolated familial dilated cardiomyopathy with impaired left ventricular systolic function.
Inherited postsynaptic neuromuscular junction dysfunction. Weakness and ptosis reflect impaired transmission; independent muscle or ocular tissue damage is not established.
EBV-associated malignant B-cell lymphoma. Extranodal sites vary; no individual additional organ is established as directly involved in at least 30%.
